notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Sources: FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0001543151-25-000008) and 2025 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001308179-25-000210), read on EDGAR. Uber's 10-K tables list years in ascending order (2022, 2023, 2024), so the 2024 value is the last number in each quote. LEADER: Khosrowshahi is a hired CEO. He beneficially owns 2,286,562 shares as of March 3, 2025 (1,166,114 held, 543,497 RSUs vesting within 60 days, 576,951 exercisable options), marked * (less than 1%), so pctEconomic is null. HOLDERS: the proxy gives only the filing dates of the 13G reports (Vanguard February 13, 2024; BlackRock January 26, 2024; Capital Research February 13, 2025), not their as-of dates, so asOf is null; percentages use the March 3, 2025 share count. STOCK COMP: 1,796 is the cash-flow add-back and the XBRL ShareBasedCompensation fact; a separate equity-statement line shows 1,847 for 2024 (equity-classified awards credited to paid-in capital), which is a different measure and is not used. GEOGRAPHY: footnote 1 to the U.K. line says that in 2022 Uber modified its arrangements in certain markets and as a result presents the respective Mobility and Delivery revenue on a gross basis (payments to drivers and couriers go into cost of revenue).

definition.quote: We define Gross Bookings as the total dollar value, including any applicable taxes, tolls, and fees, of: Mobility rides, Delivery orders (in each case without any adjustment for consumer discounts and refunds, Driver and Merchant earnings, and Driver incentives) and Freight revenue. Gross Bookings do not include tips earned by Drivers.

ecosystem.notes: Gross Bookings include Freight revenue, which Uber books gross, as well as taxes, tolls and fees. They exclude tips. Revenue includes Freight revenue. The 10-K does not state total driver or courier earnings, so payouts is null. 'Platform Participant direct transaction costs' (costs paid to Platform Earners that Uber records in cost of revenue, plus end-user incentives) are a partial, mixed amount, not total earnings, and are not used.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Uber presents revenue on a gross basis in markets where it is responsible for the Mobility, Delivery or Freight service, with payments to drivers and carriers in cost of revenue, so revenue ÷ Gross Bookings overstates what Uber keeps.
